localBiteReport: The most recent available report (September 4–10, 2026) from Great Days Outdoors, featuring Capt. Blake Nelson of Last Cast Charters, notes the first signs of fall transition across Choctawhatchee Bay, with large concentrations of bait — schools of greenies — pushing from open water into bayous, flats, bridge areas, and rolldowns. Redfish activity on the flats is described as improving and expected to strengthen further as September moves toward October; water temp is 87°F. A Santa Rosa Beach angler report on CaptainExperiences (~Sept 9) logged a 40¼-inch, 26-lb bull redfish alongside solid speckled trout numbers. A Fort Walton Beach captain also posted around the same time noting redfish and trout building in the bay as the season transitions to fall, with redfish expected to be particularly strong. No current flounder, sheepshead, or black drum catches were specifically mentioned in this week's reports, though these species are resident year-round in the bay.
